scope: Cash drawer session lifecycle + retry-on-fiscal-alloc-fail + concurrency invariants
summary: Cash drawer + fiscal sequence + audit chain hot paths share a uniform 3-layer concurrency pattern: Cache::lock for app-layer serialisation (granular per-branch/per-session keys), DB::transaction + lockForUpdate for storage-layer serialisation, UNIQUE constraint for the ultimate gate. The pattern is replicated correctly in openSession (Cache::lock(cash_drawer_open_b{N}_u{N}, 5s) + DB FOR UPDATE + UNIQUE partial WHERE status='open'), recordMovement (FOR UPDATE on session + status check + INSERT, all inside the same transaction), reconcile (FOR UPDATE + idempotent on already-reconciled), AuditLogService::write (Cache::lock 10s + retry-once on UNIQUE violation if 2 writers slipped past the cache), FiscalSequenceService::next (Cache::lock 5s + FOR UPDATE on MAX), ZReportService::open/close (Cache::lock 10s). The fiscal-alloc orphan retry pattern (migration 2026_05_09_200000) provides a graceful recovery path: if FiscalSequenceService::next throws during kiosk-paid finalize, fiscal_alloc_error_at is stamped and a cron picks the row up later — no manual operator intervention needed, no chain gap created. The audit chain write under cache outage is the only path that can race; the retry-once handler catches UNIQUE constraint violations and recomputes prev_hash + reinserts, so a 2-writer race is converted into a single ordered append.

operational_invariants_attested.invariant: I1 — Cash drawer no double-open per (branch, user)
operational_invariants_attested.evidence: CashDrawerService::openSession lines 75-99 — Cache::lock + DB FOR UPDATE + UNIQUE partial. LockTimeoutException → HTTP 409. Production-grade.

operational_invariants_attested.invariant: I4 — recordMovement refuses on non-OPEN session
operational_invariants_attested.evidence: CashDrawerService:437-444 — status check INSIDE the DB::transaction with FOR UPDATE on the session row. Race-resistant against concurrent close().

operational_invariants_attested.invariant: Fiscal sequence allocation atomic per branch
operational_invariants_attested.evidence: FiscalSequenceService::next — Cache::lock(fiscal_seq_b{N}, 5s) + DB::transaction + Order::lockForUpdate->max + 1. SQLite uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE.

operational_invariants_attested.invariant: Audit chain fork-resistant under cache outage
operational_invariants_attested.evidence: AuditLogService::performInsert lines 179-191 — catches QueryException with UNIQUE/23000/23505 code, retries once with attempt+1. Second collision propagates (real fault).

Migration 2026_05_09_200000 + FrontendOrderService (referenced) flag fiscal_alloc_error_at on failure. Cron `foodking:fiscal:retry-alloc` (referenced) picks the row up. Reset to NULL on success — column doubles as 'currently degraded' marker.

operational_invariants_attested.invariant: Hardware simulation never weakens audit/fiscal layers
operational_invariants_attested.evidence: PaymentService:296-300 downgrades strict→soft on simulation_hardware=true ONLY for the cash-drawer-session requirement. SplitPaymentService:204-218 same pattern. AuditLog write + FiscalSequenceService::next ALWAYS run.

findings.title: Cache::lock timeout values are tight — pathological-burst margin small
findings.evidence: FiscalSequenceService LOCK_TTL=5s, ACQUIRE=3s. AuditLogService LOCK_TTL=10s, ACQUIRE=5s. ZReportService LOCK_TTL=10s, ACQUIRE=4s. Under a 20+ concurrent POS checkout burst on a slow DB the audit chain lock could deny writes. Mitigation: the retry-once on UNIQUE catches the race when cache lock fails. No empirical evidence of contention but worth monitoring in production (Sprint H1 added observability via fiscal channel).
findings.verdict: KEEP-AS-IS — monitor in prod via [FISCAL_TIMING] log channel; tune up if p99 acquire latency approaches threshold

findings.title: AuditLogService chain lock release on connection death — best-effort
findings.evidence: AuditLogService:118-120 — optional($lock)->release() in finally. If the Redis connection dies between block() and release(), the lock auto-expires after CHAIN_LOCK_TTL (10s). During that window, audit_logs writes for the affected branch wait up to CHAIN_LOCK_WAIT (5s). Recovery is graceful but visible to users as a 5s delay. Mitigation: increase Redis HA OR shorten LOCK_TTL.
findings.verdict: V1.1-BACKLOG (Redis HA topology + alerting on lock timeout)

findings.title: Audit-log write failure inside cash drawer reconcile is best-effort — non-blocking
findings.evidence: CashDrawerService::writeAuditLog:534-547 catches any throw and downgrades to Log::warning. Rationale (inline): DB-layer immutability triggers + FK RESTRICT guarantee the raw fiscal evidence cannot be erased. The audit row is belt-and-suspenders. For NF525 compliance the cash_drawer_sessions row + cash_movements rows are the primary evidence; the audit_logs entry is a secondary forensic link. If audit chain is temporarily unavailable, the operation completes correctly. Reconcile auto-recovery + alerting recommended.
findings.verdict: KEEP-AS-IS — design is correct (audit best-effort, raw fiscal mandatory). V1.1: add alerting on cash audit_log.write_failed log warning.
